item.title: Loss of flat sale due to building shaking due to vibrations from poor road surface & problems caused by bus stop, 25th October
item.description:
Dear Sir or Madam,I am writing to demand urgent Council intervention regarding the poor road surface and bus stop directly outside my residential property at 84 Shoot Up Hill, NW 3XJ [Bus Stop BH – Minster Road].I have lost a property sale specifically because of the shaking of the building, associated with traffic, the deteriorating road surface and bus activity at this location. The building also has numerous cracks which may be related to these issues and I have incurred extra financial loss with the constant repair of cracks in my flat. Either way, the loss of the buyer for my flat, has already caused me significant financial loss, and I cannot accept a situation in which these problems remain unresolved without meaningful action. Let me know if you require to see proof as to why the buyer pulled out. The sale was going through with Foxtons.I therefore request an urgent, coordinated investigation and concrete action to address the following issues.1. Road deterioration, building vibration and potential structural damageThe carriageway has significant rutting, uneven surfaces and deformation. Heavy vehicles repeatedly stopping, idling and waiting nearby generate noticeable vibration.I request that the Council:Arrange an urgent highways inspection and repair the damaged carriageway.Investigate the exact cause of the building's vibration Assess whether heavy traffic, road deterioration and buses stopping or waiting at this location are contributing to the vibration and damage.Implement interim measures to reduce vibration, address safety concerns and prevent further deterioration.The loss of my property sale demonstrates the serious financial consequences of this situation. Please confirm within ten working days when the inspection and investigations will take place, what remedial action is proposed and the anticipated timescales. 2. Removal or relocation of the bus stopIn addition to point 1, I formally request that the Council assess removing or relocating the bus stop away from this residential area. The current location is causing significant disruption and concerns regarding property damage, residents' safety, security and quality of life.The bus stops in this location also appear to be excessively close together, resulting in repeated stopping, waiting and acceleration of heavy vehicles along this stretch of road. Please measure the distances between the stops and assess their spacing against relevant TfL and highway-design guidance. Confirm whether the current arrangement is appropriate and whether consolidation or relocation could reduce unnecessary stopping and its impact on residents.Please treat removal or relocation as a separate issue from road repairs. Confirm whether these options will be formally assessed, the timescale for a decision and the reasons if the request is rejected.3. Anti-social behaviour, hazardous waste and access to private propertyPeople waiting for buses regularly wander onto my private property and driveway, leaving behind used condoms, drug-related waste including needles, litter and broken glass. This is not simply anti-social behaviour occurring near the bus stop; it is taking place on private residential property, creating serious hygiene, security and safety concerns, including the risk of injury.Other recurring problems include graffiti on our property's exterior walls (which we've already spent money on repainting several times over the years), vandalism, public urination and vomiting, suspected drug use, fighting, shouting, and individuals apparently checking vehicles for unlocked doors.Buses also regularly stop and wait for extended periods, sometimes obstructing access to our residential driveway.I request that the Council coordinate with the relevant enforcement, police, highways and transport teams to:Take action to prevent people entering private property and address recurring anti-social behaviour.Arrange the safe removal of hazardous waste and consider enhanced street cleaning.Assess whether improved CCTV, enforcement or other preventative measures are appropriate.Investigate bus stopping arrangements and implement measures to maintain unobstructed residential access.Please confirm what immediate and longer-term measures will be taken. 4. Formal response, accountability and follow-upGiven the financial loss I have already suffered as a direct result of the building shaking, I require this complaint to be formally recorded and escalated to the appropriate senior officer.Please acknowledge receipt promptly and provide a substantive written response within 10 working days, confirming:Who will investigate each issue and when.The proposed technical assessments, highways repairs and interim measures.Whether removal or relocation of the bus stop will be assessed separately, including the spacing between stops.What action will be taken regarding hazardous waste, anti-social behaviour and access to private property.The timetable for remedial action and how I will receive regular progress updates.If a full investigation cannot be completed within 10 working days, please explain why, provide an interim action plan and confirm the expected completion date. If any issue falls outside your team's remit, please identify the responsible authority, refer the matter accordingly and confirm this in writing.I reserve my position regarding the financial losses I have suffered and any further losses arising from the continuation of these problems.I expect a response addressing each of the issues and specific requests above, rather than a general acknowledgement. Given the property sale I have already lost and the continuing concerns about potential building damage, urgent investigation, clear accountability and effective action are essential.Please communicate with me via email: anna@akproductions.co.uk ThanksYours faithfully,Anna KingsleyOwner of flat 3, 84 Shoot Up Hill , London NW2 3XJ& Director of 84 Shoot Up Hill RTM Ltd

item.title: Fly tipping, 24th October
item.description:
Dear Sir/Madam, I would like to report an incident of littering that I witnessed at around 8:00 am on Saturday near St Peter’s & St Paul Catholic Primary School. While I was working nearby, I saw a man throwing rubbish out of his car into the surrounding area. Unfortunately, I had left my phone in my van and was unable to take a photograph at the time. However, I managed to photograph the vehicle’s number plate as the man was leaving. It is very disappointing to see people treating our local environment in this way. Littering makes public spaces unpleasant for residents, children and other members of the community. I would be grateful if the council could investigate this incident using the information and photograph I can provide, and consider appropriate enforcement action if there is sufficient evidence. I hope action can be taken to discourage this behaviour and help keep the area clean. Kind regards
